title: "Use AKsf boundaries in GMT"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Use AKsf boundaries in GMT}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

AKsf provides the fisheries geometry; [GMT](https://www.generic-mapping-tools.org/)
provides its own cartography. `write_gmt()` writes GMT/OGR polygon files through
sf/GDAL. GMT is optional and is needed only when rendering a GMT figure.
This preserves your GMT shell workflow rather than reimplementing GMT in R.

## Export from R

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(AKsf)
write_gmt(get_fmp_areas("BSAI_GF"), "bsai.gmt")
write_gmt(get_fmp_areas("GOA_GF"), "goa.gmt")
write_gmt(get_reporting_areas(), "reporting.gmt")
write_gmt(get_coast(), "land.gmt")
```

The output uses WGS84 longitude/latitude, retains identifiers and polygon holes,
and splits multipart features and dateline crossings. Attributes repeat for each
polygon part; rows are not necessarily unique areas. Existing files require
`overwrite = TRUE`. The sf installation needs GDAL's writable GMT driver.

## Render with GMT 6

Install GMT using its [platform instructions](https://www.generic-mapping-tools.org/download/)
(for example, `brew install gmt` on macOS). PNG/PDF output also needs Ghostscript.
Run these commands in the directory containing the exported files:

```bash
gmt begin alaska-fmp png
  gmt set FONT_TITLE 16p FONT_ANNOT_PRIMARY 9p MAP_FRAME_PEN 1p
  gmt basemap -R170/235/48/72 -JB-154/50/55/65/18c -Baf -BWSne+t"Alaska groundfish FMP reference areas"
  gmt plot bsai.gmt -Glightblue -W0.4p,steelblue -l"BSAI groundfish"
  gmt plot goa.gmt -Glightgoldenrod -W0.4p,darkorange -l"GOA groundfish"
  gmt plot reporting.gmt -W0.2p,gray40
  gmt plot land.gmt -Ggray90 -W0.2p,gray50
  gmt legend -DjTR+w4.5c+o0.3c -F+gwhite+p0.25p
gmt end
```

This is a GMT Albers map with central meridian 154°W, latitude of origin 50°N,
and standard parallels 55°N/65°N. Those parameters resemble AKsf's default,
but GMT's geographic plotting is not a declaration that this figure is an
EPSG:3338 dataset: exported coordinates are WGS84. The region uses 170–235°E
so the Aleutians cross 180° continuously. Do not relabel projected metre
coordinates as longitude/latitude or discard polygon-hole markers.

The example uses bundled land rather than a remote coastline download. For
higher-resolution basemaps, use GMT's coastline/relief facilities or akgfmaps
sources with their own provenance. The fisheries boundaries remain AKsf's
cartographic references, regardless of rendering tool.

## Environmental grids

Use coldpool's temperature products as the environmental source. `terra` can
write a chosen upstream raster to a GMT-readable grid format such as GeoTIFF;
GMT's `grdimage` can render it when GMT has GDAL support. Preserve its native CRS,
missing values, registration, and units; an arbitrary projected grid is not a
longitude/latitude grid. Check `gmt grdinfo` and transform explicitly if the GMT
workflow requires geographic coordinates. Do not recompute the published
cold-pool index from an FMP mask.

See the repository's [AFSC integration guide](https://github.com/jimianelli/AKsf/blob/main/docs/AFSC-INTEGRATION.md)
for overlap with coldpool, akgfmaps, and navmaps. AKsf does not duplicate their
survey design, environmental models, or navigation exporters.

## Survey and seasonal catch case study

The [Eastern Bering Sea survey and fishery maps article](https://jimianelli.github.io/AKsf/articles/pollock-maps.html)
shows how AKsf geometry supports survey comparisons and catch columns over GMT
Earth Relief. It includes shaded log-value views, matched map planes, an
exaggerated terrain example, and simple input/update instructions. The archived
figures use supplied observations; the article's executable example uses
clearly labeled synthetic catch points and runs offline.
